# std/os.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from std/os.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The operating system's files and descriptors, clocks,
directories and readiness (poll, epoll), for programs on the hosted
target, over the `host_sys` builtin. A call that fails gives
`Option::None` or `false`, and `os_errno` says why. Descriptors are plain
numbers: nothing proves one is open, or closed only once. `host_sys` is
stage1 only and, for now, needs the C backend:
backend: c

`import "std/os.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [std/host.bastio](std-host.md).

| [`os_read`](#os_read) | Reads up to `max` bytes from `fd` into `out` (replacing it); `Some(0)` is the end of the file. |
| [`os_open`](#os_open) | Opens the file at `path` with `flags` (`OS_READ` and the others or'ed together), creating it with permission bits `perm` (0o644 is 420) when `OS_CREATE` is among them. |
| [`os_close`](#os_close) | Closes descriptor `fd`. |
| [`os_seek`](#os_seek) | Moves `fd`'s position to `off` bytes from the start; the new position. |

| [`os_time_ns`](#os_time_ns) | The time in nanoseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC (`Date.now()` is this divided by a million). |
| [`os_cpu_ns`](#os_cpu_ns) | The processor time the program has used, in nanoseconds. |
| [`os_tz`](#os_tz) | The local time zone at `secs` seconds since 1970 (UTC; a time before 1970 is its two's complement), from the `TZ` variable or the system's zone files. |

| [`os_tz_west`](#os_tz_west) | How many seconds west of UTC the zone `os_tz` returned is (0 if it is east). |

## Types and constants

### `OS_FAIL`

```bastio
const OS_FAIL: u64 = 18446744073709551615;
```

### `OS_TZ_BIAS`

```bastio
const OS_TZ_BIAS: u64 = 172800;
```

Added to the offset `os_tz` returns, so that a zone west of UTC is not negative.

### `OS_TZ_DST`

```bastio
const OS_TZ_DST: u64 = 4294967296;
```

Added to what `os_tz` returns while summer time is in force.

### `OS_READ`

```bastio
const OS_READ: u64 = 1;
```

Open for reading (`os_open` flags; or them together).

### `OS_WRITE`

```bastio
const OS_WRITE: u64 = 2;
```

Open for writing.

### `OS_CREATE`

```bastio
const OS_CREATE: u64 = 4;
```

Create the file if it does not exist.

### `OS_TRUNC`

```bastio
const OS_TRUNC: u64 = 8;
```

Cut the file to nothing.

### `OS_APPEND`

```bastio
const OS_APPEND: u64 = 16;
```

Write at the end.

### `OS_EXCL`

```bastio
const OS_EXCL: u64 = 32;
```

With `OS_CREATE`: fail if the file exists.

### `Stat`

```bastio
struct Stat { kind: u64, size: u64, perm: u64, mtime: u64, atime: u64, ctime: u64, dev: u64, ino: u64 }
```

What `os_stat` says about a file: its kind (1 file, 2 directory, 3
symbolic link, 4 other), its size in bytes, its permission bits, the
times its contents and status last changed and it was last read (in
nanoseconds since 1970), and its device and inode numbers.

## Functions

### `os_errno`

```bastio
fn os_errno(h: &Host) -> u64
```

The error number (`errno`) of the last call of this module that failed.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("no/such/file");
let s = os_stat(host, p);
bfree(p);
if !(s is Option::None) || os_errno(host) != 2 { return 1; }   // ENOENT
```

### `os_write_all`

```bastio
fn os_write_all(h: &Host, fd: u64, data: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Writes `data` to descriptor `fd` (1 is standard output, 2 standard
error), retrying after a partial write; false if it cannot all be written.

Example:

```bastio
let s = bfrom("");
let ok = os_write_all(host, 1, s);
bfree(s);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `os_print`

```bastio
fn os_print(h: &Host, text: &Bytes)
```

Writes `text` to standard output (what `console.log` needs).

Example:

```bastio
let s = bfrom("");
os_print(host, s);
bfree(s);
```

### `os_read`

```bastio
fn os_read(h: &Host, fd: u64, max: u64, out: &mut Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Reads up to `max` bytes from `fd` into `out` (replacing it); `Some(0)`
is the end of the file.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("os_read.tmp");
let d = bfrom("abc");
let wrote = write_file(host, p, d);
let mut got = balloc(0);
let mut n = 99;
match os_open(host, p, OS_READ, 0) {
  Option::Some(fd) => {
    match os_read(host, fd, 2, &mut got) {
      Option::Some(k) => { n = k; },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    os_close(host, fd);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
os_unlink(host, p);
let ok = wrote && n == 2 && blen(got) == 2;
bfree(got); bfree(d); bfree(p);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `os_open`

```bastio
fn os_open(h: &Host, path: &Bytes, flags: u64, perm: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Opens the file at `path` with `flags` (`OS_READ` and the others or'ed
together), creating it with permission bits `perm` (0o644 is 420) when
`OS_CREATE` is among them. The descriptor is closed on exec.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("os_open.tmp");
let mut ok = false;
match os_open(host, p, OS_WRITE | OS_CREATE | OS_TRUNC, 420) {
  Option::Some(fd) => { ok = os_close(host, fd); },
  Option::None => {},
}
os_unlink(host, p);
bfree(p);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `os_close`

```bastio
fn os_close(h: &Host, fd: u64) -> bool
```

Closes descriptor `fd`.

Example:

```bastio
if os_close(host, 999999) { return 1; }   // not open
```

### `os_seek`

```bastio
fn os_seek(h: &Host, fd: u64, off: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Moves `fd`'s position to `off` bytes from the start; the new position.

Example:

```bastio
if os_seek(host, 999999, 0) is Option::Some { return 1; }
```

### `os_mono_ns`

```bastio
fn os_mono_ns(h: &Host) -> u64
```

The monotonic clock in nanoseconds (for measuring time and timers; its
zero is some moment in the past).

Example:

```bastio
let a = os_mono_ns(host);
let b = os_mono_ns(host);
if b < a { return 1; }
```

### `os_time_ns`

```bastio
fn os_time_ns(h: &Host) -> u64
```

The time in nanoseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC (`Date.now()` is this
divided by a million).

Example:

```bastio
if os_time_ns(host) < 1700000000000000000 { return 1; }
```

### `os_cpu_ns`

```bastio
fn os_cpu_ns(h: &Host) -> u64
```

The processor time the program has used, in nanoseconds.

Example:

```bastio
if os_cpu_ns(host) == OS_FAIL { return 1; }
```

### `os_tz`

```bastio
fn os_tz(h: &Host, secs: u64, name: &mut Bytes) -> u64
```

The local time zone at `secs` seconds since 1970 (UTC; a time before 1970
is its two's complement), from the `TZ` variable or the system's zone
files: `name` is replaced with its abbreviation (such as `JST`), and the
result is the offset east of UTC in seconds plus `OS_TZ_BIAS`, with
`OS_TZ_DST` added while summer time is in force (`OS_FAIL` if it cannot be
told). `os_tz_east` and `os_tz_west` take the offset apart.

Example:

```bastio
let mut name = balloc(0);
let z = os_tz(host, 1700000000, &mut name);
bfree(name);
if z == OS_FAIL { return 1; }
if os_tz_east(z) > 93600 || os_tz_west(z) > 93600 { return 1; }
```

### `os_tz_east`

```bastio
fn os_tz_east(z: u64) -> u64
```

How many seconds east of UTC the zone `os_tz` returned is (0 if it is west).

Example:

```bastio
if os_tz_east(OS_TZ_BIAS + 32400) != 32400 { return 1; }
```

### `os_tz_west`

```bastio
fn os_tz_west(z: u64) -> u64
```

How many seconds west of UTC the zone `os_tz` returned is (0 if it is east).

Example:

```bastio
if os_tz_west(OS_TZ_BIAS - 18000 + OS_TZ_DST) != 18000 { return 1; }
```

### `os_stat_at`

```bastio
fn os_stat_at(h: &Host, path: &Bytes, follow: bool) -> Option[Stat]
```

What the file at `path` is (following symbolic links when `follow`).

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom(".");
let r = os_stat_at(host, p, true);
bfree(p);
match r {
  Option::Some(s) => { if s.kind != 2 { return 1; } },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `os_stat`

```bastio
fn os_stat(h: &Host, path: &Bytes) -> Option[Stat]
```

What the file at `path` is, following symbolic links.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("std/os.bastio");
let r = os_stat(host, p);
bfree(p);
match r {
  Option::Some(s) => { if s.kind != 1 || s.size == 0 { return 1; } },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `os_list`

```bastio
fn os_list(h: &Host, path: &Bytes, out: &mut Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

The entries of the directory at `path` (not `.` and `..`), into `out`
(replacing it): each is its kind byte (as `Stat.kind`), its name and a
zero byte. The result is how many there are.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("std");
let mut names = balloc(0);
let n = os_list(host, p, &mut names);
let ok = n is Option::Some && blen(names) > 0;
bfree(names); bfree(p);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

```bastio
fn os_isatty(h: &Host, fd: u64) -> bool
```

### `os_pipe`

```bastio
fn os_pipe(h: &Host) -> Option[Span]
```

A pipe: its read end and its write end, both closed on exec.

Example:

```bastio
match os_pipe(host) {
  Option::Some(p) => { os_close(host, p.start); os_close(host, p.end); },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `os_nonblock`

```bastio
fn os_nonblock(h: &Host, fd: u64, on: bool) -> bool
```

Makes reads and writes on `fd` return at once (failing with EAGAIN, 11
on Linux) instead of waiting, or wait again. False on Windows, which has no
such mode for these descriptors.

Example:

```bastio
match os_pipe(host) {
  Option::Some(p) => {
    let ok = os_nonblock(host, p.start, true);
    let mut got = balloc(0);
    let mut bad = false;
    if ok {   // (Windows cannot: reading would wait for ever)
      bad = os_read(host, p.start, 8, &mut got) is Option::Some;   // nothing written yet
    }
    bfree(got);
    os_close(host, p.start); os_close(host, p.end);
    if bad { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `os_poll`

```bastio
fn os_poll(h: &Host, fds: &mut Bytes, ms: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Waits until one of the descriptors in `fds` is ready or `ms`
milliseconds pass (`OS_FAIL`: no limit). `fds` holds 8 bytes a
descriptor, little endian: the descriptor (32 bits), the events to wait
for (16 bits: 1 input, 4 output) and the events that happened (16 bits,
filled in). The result is how many are ready. On Windows it is `None`.

Example:

```bastio
match os_pipe(host) {
  Option::Some(p) => {
    let mut fds = balloc(8);
    bset(&mut fds, 0, cast[u8](p.end & 255));
    bset(&mut fds, 4, 4);   // POLLOUT
    let n = os_poll(host, &mut fds, 0);
    let mut ready: u8 = 0;
    if blen(fds) == 8 { ready = bget(fds, 6); }
    bfree(fds);
    os_close(host, p.start); os_close(host, p.end);
    if n is Option::Some && ready != 4 { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

## Internals

### `os_word`

```bastio
fn os_word(r: &Bytes, i: u64) -> u64
  requires blen(r) == 64 && i < 8
```

Internal: the word at `i` of an eight-word stat record.

### `os_path_op`

```bastio
fn os_path_op(h: &Host, op: u64, path: &Bytes, a: u64) -> bool
```

Internal: one of the operations on a path that only succeed or fail.
